There is no single nationwide date when the United States “got rid of” the electric chair, because states ended or limited its use at different times. Nebraska effectively abolished the electric chair in February 2008 when its Supreme Court ruled electrocution unconstitutional [d5,d6]. New York stopped using it in 1963 [d8], and nationally electrocution has largely been supplanted by lethal injection since the late 20th century, though some states still retain it as an option for certain condemned inmates [d2,d4,d9,d10].
